A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCScore study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original diversity-correlation experiments, human and GPT-4 evaluations, computational timings, downstream classification results, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds colored-MNIST evaluation, duplicate-sample robustness experiments, and timing comparisons with FKEA methods.

M1.justification: The main embedding–kernel–softmax–trace procedure remains unchanged. However, v2 removes DCScorecluster from v1 Appendix C.1, an alternative procedure restricting similarities and classification probabilities to samples within the same K-means cluster. Section 4.1 now leaves alternative implementations to future work.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from text to colored-MNIST images, using label count as diversity ground truth (Section 5.5.2). It also introduces duplicate-contaminated versions of the retained AttrPrompt datasets as a robustness scenario (Section 5.5.3). The original text tasks and datasets remain.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2 and Table 12 add actual timing comparisons against FKEA-Vendi and FKEA-RKE, substantially extending the efficiency comparison to accelerated entropy-based methods. Distinct-n, K-means Inertia, and VendiScore remain in the corresponding original comparisons. Standalone RKE is discussed but is not a separate evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate images with Inception V3 and Dino V2, normalize scores by each method's maximum, and inject 0–6,000 duplicates into text datasets. Appendix C.2.1 also changes the stated default kernel for DCScore and VendiScore from cosine similarity to inner product. This establishes a reported setting revision, but does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled tests of diversity-score stability under duplicate injection (Table 8) and consistency across two image embedders (Figure 6). These address robustness questions beyond the original analyses. Existing temperature sensitivity, text-embedding/kernel sensitivity, and downstream training analyses remain after renumbering.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix D.2 newly specify different random seeds for data sampling in the FKEA timing comparison. Existing five-repeat evaluations and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain. The expanded human-evaluation description does not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Figure 6 and Tables 8 and 12 add image-diversity, duplication-stability, and efficiency results. For example, Table 12 reports 64k-sample SST2 timings of 90.36 seconds for DCScore versus 295.14 for FKEA-Vendi, but Yelp timings of 641.60 versus 422.51 seconds. These are new comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings. Tables 3–7 and the matched original appendix result tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects duplicate-copy indexing from 2i to n+i, including the corresponding probability entry in the identical-samples proof. v1's piecewise mathematical definition of DCScorecluster, Equation 18, is removed. The main DCScore definition, four axioms, and complexity derivations otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 removes the conclusion's claim that existing methods can be unified within DCScore, although the corresponding baseline formulations remain in renamed Appendix E. The introduction newly foregrounds the already-present complexity analysis as a contribution. The abstract's central method, axiomatic, correlation, and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 changes the low-diversity explanation from classification into one category to random classification, adds interpretations of duplicate robustness and image-encoder consistency, and discusses why end-to-end timing may limit FKEA's benefit. The conclusion explicitly identifies direct image-text evaluation as unsupported because multimodal representation extraction and fusion remain unresolved.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2.5 explicitly documents 15 pairwise comparisons, 45 judgments across three evaluators, and ranking aggregation for the existing human evaluation. v2 also clarifies evaluation of generated components and supplies image-encoder settings and FKEA alpha values. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, generation prompts, and code-access information are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning around RKE and FKEA and adds related work on precision/recall, density/coverage, and out-of-distribution robustness. Its bibliography also adds the MNIST reference and removes Wang et al. (2018), Additive Margin Softmax. These are targeted extensions within the retained literature-review framework.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology corrections, including 'Preliminaries,' and expands several explanations. Section 5.5 becomes three subsections; the clustering appendix disappears, later appendices are relabeled, and human-evaluation, limitation, acknowledgement, and impact passages are added. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order remain.

P2.justification: v2 enlarges and redraws Figure 1 across both columns, cleans up Figure 2, and adjusts Figure 4's tick labeling. It adds the colored-MNIST plot and duplicate/FKEA result tables. Existing displays are largely retained, with relocation, caption editing, and renumbering rather than a comprehensive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical scrutiny through visual and duplicate-robustness checks and more relevant efficiency comparators, including the unfavorable Yelp outcome in Table 12. Clearer human-evaluation documentation, the proof-indexing correction, and the explicit multimodal limitation also help. These gains outweigh the loss of the unvalidated clustering alternative. However, the new inference that lower VendiScore values imply underestimated diversity (Table 8) lacks independent ground truth, limiting the overall improvement.
